validation.notes: Repaired the authorization-to-effect chain across three real modules and verified it with .prale-eval/regression.mjs (loaded through the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs helper, which links the submitted TypeScript modules; only the checkpoint store, the progress transport and the outcome publisher are boundary fakes). Fixes: (1) packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts recoverToolInvocation now requires !cancelled && tool !== undefined && call.replay === "safe" && tool.replay === "safe", so both replay declarations must be safe and a missing tool stays interrupted instead of executing; (2) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/effect-gate.ts createGate().gate.admit now calls the existing check() before invoking, so an aborting gate throws AbortRequested with its cancellation promise and a closed gate throws its fault before any effect starts; (3) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/tools.ts executeToolCall now passes call.args (the cleared/validated/persisted arguments) to tool.execute instead of call.toolCall.arguments. Observed cross-module behaviour asserted: clear-before-invoke, effect-complete -> seal -> drain -> drain-complete -> publish ordering, no publish while a deferred durable progress drain is still pending, persisted arguments reaching the tool (default and custom effect), cancelled recovery publishing the interruption marker with the kept checkpoint and no clear/invoke, unsafe declarations on either side and missing tools staying interrupted, aborting gate refusing admission without invoking, and a closed gate propagating its fault with zero effects. Mutation check: restoring each faulty baseline alone (effect-gate.ts, execution/tools.ts, runtime/drive/tools.ts) made the script fail with an uncaught node:assert/strict AssertionError, not a crash, import error or timeout. No temporary inputs are created, so nothing to clean up; vitest/typescript are not installed in this workspace, so the repo's own vitest suites and tsc type-check could not be run as extra evidence.
